clinicalPearls: Presents as multiple small, smooth, skin-coloured to yellowish dermal cysts, often on the chest, axillae, trunk and proximal limbs
The cysts arise from the sebaceous duct and characteristically discharge an oily or creamy fluid when incised
Familial cases are autosomal dominant and caused by variants in KRT17 (keratin 17), which is also implicated in pachyonychia congenita type 2
It may overlap with pachyonychia congenita type 2, so nail changes and natal teeth should be sought in KRT17-related disease
Steatocystoma multiplex suppurativa describes a variant in which cysts become inflamed, rupture and scar, resembling acne conglobata or hidradenitis
Diagnosis is clinical, confirmed if needed by biopsy showing a cyst wall with an eosinophilic corrugated cuticle and sebaceous gland lobules within or adjacent to the wall
Management is largely cosmetic and includes expression or excision of individual cysts and treatment of inflamed lesions
reference.pathophysiology: Steatocystoma multiplex is a naevoid malformation of the pilosebaceous unit centred on the sebaceous duct. In familial disease, dominant variants in KRT17 disturb the keratin cytoskeleton of the sebaceous duct and associated epithelium, producing multiple cysts lined by stratified squamous epithelium with a characteristic crenulated eosinophilic cuticle and containing sebaceous lobules. The cysts accumulate sebaceous secretions, and when they rupture the released contents provoke inflammation, which in the suppurativa variant leads to abscess-like lesions and scarring.
additionalInvestigations: Skin biopsy of a cyst showing the corrugated eosinophilic cuticle and sebaceous lobules
Molecular genetic testing of KRT17 in familial cases
Assessment for pachyonychia congenita features (nails, natal teeth, oral leucokeratosis)
Bacterial swab of inflamed or suppurative lesions
redFlags: Extensive suppurative disease with abscess formation and disfiguring scarring
Rapid change in a longstanding lesion suggesting an alternative diagnosis
Recurrent secondary infection requiring repeated intervention
Significant psychological distress from cosmetic burden
reference.prognosis: The condition is benign with no malignant potential; cysts persist and slowly accumulate over time, and the main impact is cosmetic, though the suppurativa variant can cause scarring.
pitfalls: Overlooking the association with KRT17 and pachyonychia congenita type 2
Attempting complete surgical clearance of numerous cysts with resulting scarring
Mistaking inflamed cysts for acne or hidradenitis and missing the underlying diagnosis
Failing to counsel on the chronic, recurring nature of the disorder
management: Benign condition needing no treatment for asymptomatic cysts, with reassurance regarding the absence of malignant potential
Surgical excision, incision and drainage, or mini-incision extraction for troublesome or cosmetically significant cysts
Ablative laser or cryotherapy and electrosurgery for numerous small lesions
For the suppurativa variant, anti-inflammatory tetracycline antibiotics and, in severe scarring disease, oral isotretinoin, treating as for inflammatory acne or hidradenitis
Assess for associated pachyonychia congenita type 2 features such as nail changes and natal teeth in KRT17-related disease
Genetic counselling in familial autosomal dominant cases
